subject: Fwd: Fathom Labs — reservation checkpoint & sprint MAP
messages:
From: Tanya Rao <tanya@fathomlabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureCloud <procure@procurecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity reservation & evaluation plan — Fathom Labs

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Fathom is targeting a pilot in Q3 and we need a short mutual action plan (MAP) so Procurement can start internal approvals. High-level asks:

- We expect to run 3 active environments (dev, staging, prod) with peak prod concurrency around 1200 tokens/sec.
- Want to understand Dedicated vs Private lead times (procurement stacks and on-prem options).
- Need a recommended GPU pool sizing + tolerance for burst (20%).
- Acceptance criteria for the eval (latency SLOs, throughput tests, data path validation).

Can you share a draft MAP with milestones and owners? Procurement copied ProcureCloud here — if you can include a checklist for contracts / SOC2 evidence / SOW items that would help speed legal review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that’s easier.

— Tanya
Tanya Rao
Head of ML Ops, Fathom Labs
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tanya Rao <tanya@fathomlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ProcureCloud <procure@procurecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity reservation & evaluation plan — Fathom Labs

Hi Tanya — great to meet yesterday. Draft MAP attached (Fathom_MAP_v1.1.xlsx) — below is an executive summary and proposed timing. I pulled in Ben (serving runtime) and Marissa (customer success) to own handoff and procurement coordination.

Executive MAP (proposed) — milestones, owners, target dates
- Q: Kickoff & scoping call (owner: Neha) — target: 2027-04-26 — agenda: target latency SLO, data symlink, security boundaries
- POC / Eval window (owner: Ben) — target start: 2027-05-02, duration: 2 weeks — acceptance: 95th pct latency < 120ms on 2k token sequences, throughput >= 1.0K tokens/sec sustained for 10m windows
- Procurement & contract execution (owner: Marissa + ProcureCloud) — target: sign by 2027-06-15 — includes reserved capacity tier and support SLAs
- Capacity provisioning (owner: Infra + Ben) — Dedicated pool provisioning lead time: 10–12 weeks from contract signature; Private (on-prem) edge lead time: 14–18 weeks (includes hardware procurement and network validation)
- Staging buffer & burst plan (owner: Ben) — provision +20% headroom for first 8 weeks; automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant if needed
- Acceptance & production cutover (owner: Neha + Marissa) — target: 2027-07-15

Sizing guidance (initial estimate)
- Baseline prod concurrency: 1200 tokens/sec -> recommend 4 x A100-class machines for low-latency workloads (quantized LLM variant) with autoscale to 6 for peak bursts (20% buffer)
- If using Dedicated vCPU-backed MPS-style preemption: recommend 2x smaller machines for staging + 1 small dev node
- We included a CSV (GPU-sizing-estimate-v2.csv) with assumptions and token distribution percentiles — please review and flag any mismatch.

Procurement checklist (short)
- Signed SOW or committed capacity addendum
- SOC2 report + network architecture diagram
- Data retention / deletion requirements for Private deployments
- IP and model usage language for POC / Eval

Next steps: Please confirm target dates and acceptance criteria or propose adjustments. I can book the kickoff for 4/26 or 4/27.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tanya Rao <tanya@fathomlabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ProcureCloud <procure@procurecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity reservation & evaluation plan — Fathom Labs

Looping in technical detail from the runtime side — quick notes and a small ask to tune estimates in the attached CSV.

- Kernel & quantization notes: If Fathom will accept int8 quantized weights for the POC we can reduce GPU memory footprint ~40% which lowers required instance count. For production latency-sensitive endpoints we recommend mixed precision (fp16) on 80% of traffic and int8 fallbacks for low-cost tiers.
- Batching: Target batch windows of 12–16ms for interactive queries; this keeps 95th P99 latency within SLOs while maintaining throughput.
- KV cache strategy: We’ll enable prefix KV cache for conversation workloads — expectation is 12–18% reduction in repeated-token cost after warmup.

Operational consideration (lead times)
- Dedicated pool (cloud-hosted): procurement + infra provisioning typically 10–12 weeks. If Fathom requires specific GPU SKUs (e.g., H100 80GB), lead times can increase to 14+ weeks depending on supply.
- Private (customer on-prem): planning should include 2–3 weeks for rack/network validation plus typical hardware lead time (12–16 weeks) — plan 14–18 weeks overall.

Low-risk recommendation: Begin contract discussions now to align on reserved-capacity tranche schedule. If you want to shorten lead time, propose a staggered tranche approach: deliver minimal prod footprint first (2 GPUs) then scale to full pool across 6–8 weeks.

Attachment: GPU-sizing-estimate-v2.csv (includes per-seq estimates, memory headroom, and latency-stress test plan)

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Tanya Rao <tanya@fathomlabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureCloud <procure@procurecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity reservation & evaluation plan — Fathom Labs

Neha / Ben / Marissa — thank you, this is exactly what Procurement needed. A few clarifications before we lock the MAP: 

- Acceptance tweak: can we change the POC latency acceptance to 95th < 140ms (we have heavier token sequences in a subset of models) — otherwise happy with throughput targets.
- Hardware SKU: Fathom prefers H100-class for peak research workloads. Ben — supply-note acknowledged; can we include a tranche schedule in the SOW that allows H100 for 30% of capacity and A100 variants for the remainder to reduce lead risk?
- DocuSign: Procurement prefers an addendum for reserved capacity. Can Marissa send a draft addendum and the DocuSign link when ready?

If those three items are acceptable, we’ll mark the MAP approved internally and instruct ProcureCloud to start the legal queue. Next step from our side: kick off the POC week of 5/2.

Thanks — Tanya
